title: Accounts Receivable Assistant
description:
Morgan McKinley are a growing international business to recruit an Accounts Receivable & Billing Assistant on a fixed-term contract.

This is a hands-on opportunity for someone with experience in billing, accounts receivable or credit control to take ownership of the end-to-end billing and collections process across multiple entities and currencies.

Key Responsibilities:
- Prepare and issue accurate client invoices, ensuring billing schedules are up to date.
- Manage aged debt, proactively chasing outstanding payments by phone and email.
- Allocate incoming receipts, including multi-currency payments, and reconcile the sales ledger.
- Resolve billing queries and liaise with internal stakeholders and clients.
- Produce aged debt and cash collection reports.
- Support month-end reconciliations and identify opportunities to improve processes.

About you:
- 2+ years' experience in billing, accounts receivable or credit control.
- Available on immediate notice, to start at short notice
- Background in a service-based business such as professional services, recruitment, consultancy, legal or SaaS.
- Strong communication skills and confidence dealing with senior client contacts.
- Excellent attention to detail and good Excel skills, including lookups and pivot tables.
- Experience with Xero and multi-currency invoicing is advantageous but not essential.

title: Junior Finance & Operations Assistant
description:
Junior Finance & Business Operations Assistant

Location: Aldermaston, Berkshire UK Salary: 27,000

This Junior Finance & Business Operations Assistant role is ideal for someone looking to develop a long-term career in finance, with hands-on experience across sales ledger, purchase ledger, credit control, and wider business operations.

The successful candidate will be organised, hardworking, and detail-oriented, with a proactive approach and a willingness to learn. This role offers the opportunity to develop practical finance skills, gain exposure to business operations, and progress towards a more senior or management position over time.

Key Responsibilities
- Finance Administration: Provide day-to-day support to the finance function, maintaining accurate financial records and assisting with reporting, reconciliations, and general finance administration.
- Sales Ledger: Assist with raising sales invoices, allocating customer payments, monitoring outstanding balances, and supporting credit control activities.
- Purchase Ledger: Process supplier invoices, check and reconcile supplier statements, maintain accurate purchase ledger records, and assist with supplier payment processes.
- Credit Control: Help monitor overdue accounts, follow up outstanding payments, and support the maintenance of healthy customer accounts.
- Business Operations & HR Support: Support HR and administrative activities, including employee record-keeping, recruitment coordination, document preparation, and coordination across business functions.

Key Requirements
- A degree in Finance, Accounting, or a related subject would be advantageous.
- An AAT Level 2 qualification, or willingness to work towards one, would be beneficial.
- Strong English and Maths skills, ideally with GCSE grades of 6 or above.
- A hardworking, reliable attitude and a genuine willingness to learn.
- An interest in developing a long-term career in finance and business operations.
- Good communication skills and the ability to work effectively with colleagues, customers, and suppliers.

Career Development

This is an excellent opportunity for someone at the start of their career to gain practical experience across core finance functions, particularly sales and purchase ledger, credit control, and business operations. With training, experience, and continued development, there is potential to progress into a more senior finance position or management role in the future.

To apply for this Junior Finance & Business Operations Assistant role based in Aldermaston, Berkshire, please send your CV to (url removed) or call (phone number removed).

title: Junior Finance Assistant

If you're looking to take the next step in your finance career and want to build your experience within a supportive finance team, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Purchase Ledger Assistant
description:
Purchase Ledger Assistant

Location: Berkshire area (office-based 4 days)
Department: Finance

About the Role

An established organisation is seeking a detail-oriented Purchase Ledger Assistant to join its Finance team. This role plays a key part in ensuring supplier invoices, subcontractor payments, reconciliations, and financial records are processed accurately and efficiently.

Working closely with operational and support teams across the business, you will provide proactive support while maintaining high standards of accuracy and compliance.

Key Responsibilities
- Process weekly self-billed subcontractor payments and invoices
- Process supplier invoices and payments in a timely manner
- Manage and resolve expense-related queries through expense management systems
- Complete supplier reconciliations, including open orders, GRNI (Goods Received Not Invoiced), and supplier statements
- Liaise with operational teams to ensure invoices are processed promptly
- Allocate direct debits, standing orders, and other electronic payments
- Monitor and resolve debit balance issues
- Ensure all processing complies with internal controls and company policies
- Respond to supplier and internal stakeholder queries efficiently and professionally
- Maintain process documentation and records
- Provide support and cover for colleagues during periods of absence
- Assist with ad hoc finance projects and additional duties as required

About You

To be successful in this role, you will have:
- Previous Purchase Ledger / Accounts Payable experience
- Experience working in a high-volume processing environment
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel
- Strong attention to detail and accuracy
- Excellent organisational skills with the ability to meet deadlines
- A proactive and team-focused approach
- Strong communication and problem-solving skills
- A commitment to maintaining high standards and delivering quality work

What We're Looking For
- Someone who enjoys working as part of a collaborative team
- The ability to follow established procedures and controls
- A positive, flexible attitude and willingness to support colleagues
- A commitment to getting things right first time

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Purchase Ledger professional looking to join a busy finance function where accuracy, teamwork, and continuous improvement are highly valued

By applying you will be registered as a candidate with Marc Daniels Specialist Recruitment Limited. Our Privacy Policy is available on our website and explains how we will use your personal data.

title: Temporary Credit Control
description:

This role requires an experienced credit controller who has solid administration skills, has worked in a process driven credit department, and is a confident and strong communicator.

Urgent requirement, must be available to start ASAP, based on site 5 days a week, 37.5 hours a week, great credit controller and fantastic team player!

Logistics experience ideal but not essential.

title: Accounts Assistant
description:
As an Accounts Assistant, you will support the day-to-day financial operations of a retail business, processing transactions, maintaining accurate records, and assisting with budgeting, reconciliations, and financial reporting. Working closely with finance, marketing, and external partners, you will help ensure costs are recorded correctly, resolve account queries, and provide reliable administrative support to keep the finance function running smoothly.

Client Details
- Established international organisation
- Operates in the retail industry
- Located in Reading

Description

Accounts Assistant responsibilities:
- Maintain accurate financial records, ensuring all accounting information, cost entries, and supporting documentation are up to date and well organised
- Process day-to-day finance administration, including the creation and maintenance of budgets, posting financial transactions, and updating records within finance systems
- Monitor and track spend against budgets, working closely with internal stakeholders to ensure financial data is recorded accurately and reported effectively
- Generate and process customer credit notes, cost recharges, and other financial adjustments in line with agreed procedures and deadlines
- Analyse financial data to identify discrepancies, investigate variances, and support the resolution of account, vendor, and customer queries
- Assist with month-end activities, reconciliations, reporting, and ensuring income and expenditure are accurately accounted for
- Support promotional and commercial activities by maintaining relevant financial records, monitoring spend, and ensuring compliance with internal processes
- Collaborate with colleagues across finance and wider business functions to ensure tasks are completed accurately, efficiently, and within required timescales
- Provide clear and professional support to internal and external stakeholders, responding to finance-related queries and helping to maintain strong working relationships

Profile

A successful Accounts Assistant should have:
- Previous experience in an Accounts Assistant, Finance Assistant, or similar finance administration role, with a strong understanding of day-to-day accounting processes
- Confident maintaining accurate financial records, processing transactions, and handling sensitive financial information with a high level of attention to detail
- Strong analytical skills with the ability to review financial data, identify discrepancies, investigate variances, and resolve issues efficiently
- Microsoft Excel skills, including the use of Pivot Tables, VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, reconciliations, and data analysis
- Experience using finance systems such as SAP or similar ERP systems
- Excellent organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and maintain accuracy
- Strong communication and stakeholder management skills
- Proactive and self-motivated, able to work independently while contributing effectively as part of a collaborative team
- A solid understanding of core accounting principles, including budgeting, reconciliations, financial reporting, and month-end processes

Job Offer

Accounts Assistant:
- Salary: 34,000 to 37,000 per annum - dependent on experience
- Competitive benefits package (TBC)
- Reading location, well-connected by public transport
- Hybrid working
- A supportive and inclusive workplace culture

title: Credit Controller
description:
As a Credit Controller in Reading, you will manage customer accounts and help keep the accounting and finance function running smoothly within the retail industry. You will maintain accurate records, follow up outstanding balances and provide clear account information to support day-to-day decisions.

Client Details
- Operates in the Retail industry
- Innovative organisation
- Great team culture
- Located in Reading

Description

Credit Controller responsibilities:
- Manage the accounts receivable and credit control process for a portfolio of customer accounts, ensuring records remain accurate and up to date.
- Chase outstanding debt by phone and email, ensuring payments are received within agreed terms and negotiating payment plans where required.
- Resolve customer account queries, including invoice discrepancies, payment disputes, pricing queries and short payments.
- Allocate and reconcile incoming payments, maintaining accurate customer ledgers and investigating any outstanding items.
- Conduct credit checks and monitor customer credit exposure, making recommendations on credit limits and account status where appropriate.
- Take ownership of the aged debt ledger, monitoring overdue balances, analysing payment trends and identifying potential risks.
- Prepare aged debt and collection reports, providing regular updates to the Finance team.
- Build strong relationships with customers and internal teams to resolve issues quickly and minimise outstanding debt.
- Support month-end activities, including reconciliations, credit notes, adjustments and cash postings.
- Identify opportunities to improve processes and provide wider support to the Finance team as required

Profile

The successful Credit Controller should have:
- Previous experience within Credit Control, Accounts Receivable, Sales Ledger or a similar finance function.
- A proven track record of managing customer accounts and reducing overdue debt.
- Confidence communicating with customers and internal stakeholders to resolve payment queries and account issues.
- Experience investigating payment discrepancies, disputes and reconciliations through to resolution.
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to prioritise workloads and manage multiple accounts effectively.
- Good analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to review payment trends and identify potential risks.
- Experience maintaining accurate customer records and preparing reports on aged debt and collection activity.
- Strong Microsoft Excel skills, including Pivot Tables and VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP functions.
- Experience using ERP or accounting systems such as SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Sage or similar finance platforms.

Job Offer

Credit Controller:
- Salary: 30,000 to 34,000 per annum - dependent on experience
- Competitive benefits package (TBC)
- Reading location, well-connected by public transport
- Hybrid working
- A supportive and inclusive workplace culture
